source_text: Pro hoc igitur Deo meo, quem mihi qualem credo omnis creatura et sancta Scriptura denuntiat, rectius dixi facerem, si nec librorum te concertatione dignum putarem. Verum quoniam mihi potissimum hoc a sanctis viris, nostri temporis confessoribus, munus impositum est, ut dicta tua quid habeant ponderis rationisque discutiam, opportunum fuit ostendere prius, non a te credi ei Deo, qui in Catholicorum semper Ecclesia praedicatus est et usque ad finem ubi illa fuerit praedicabitur.
pass_a_gloss: For this God of mine therefore, whom all creation and holy Scripture announce to me such as I believe, I said I would do more rightly, if I did not think you worthy even of a contest of books. But since this office has been imposed on me especially by holy men, confessors of our time, that I shake out what weight and reason your sayings have, it was opportune to show first that that God is not believed by you, who has always been preached in the Church of the Catholics and until the end, where that Church shall have been, will be preached.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: For this God of mine, whom all creation and Holy Scripture proclaim to me as I believe him to be, I said I would act more rightly if I did not consider you worthy even of a contest in books. But holy men, the confessors of our time, have assigned this task particularly to me: to examine what weight and reason your statements contain. It was therefore appropriate to show first that you do not believe in the God who has always been proclaimed in the Church of the catholics and will continue to be proclaimed wherever that Church is found, until the end.

choices.why: Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
